correctness.rationale: A geometric H-fixed simplex cannot contain a vertex in any moved row: its orbit includes two rooks in the same forbidden column. Thus only the k individually H-fixed unit-capacity rows plus the heavy row remain, yielding Y_{m,k} exactly, where k<=2 for nonidentity H<=S4. Every Y_{m,k} facet uses all capacities, has dimension m-5+k and satisfies shellability condition of Jojić–Vrećica–Živaljević Theorem 4.4: m >= (m-4+k)+(k+1)-1 = m-4+2k for k<=2. Direct face count f_{j-1}=sum_{a+b=j} C(k,a)(m)_a C(m-a,b), 0<=b<=m-4, and alternating-binomial Euler identity give beta0=C(m-1,3), beta1=mC(m-2,2)-C(m-1,3), beta2=m(m-3)+C(m-1,3). Independent face-count Euler checks for all 12 pairs 5<=m<=8,k<=2 passed. For ambient Z/3 torsion, Limonchenko–Yu arXiv:2610.37827 Theorem 5.7 and pages 19–20 explicitly prove a unique Z/3 via their integral relative cokernel (5.10), with generator tau=sum_{|D|=3}R^{(2)}_{D,min D} (5.11) and relations q^(2)=-q^(3). Transposition of second/third unit rows interchanges the (2),(3) families, mapping tau to -tau, hence full S4 sign. Every R^{(2)} summand is an exterior word with exactly one factor per column; any column permutation contributes its global sign on the m factors, and relation independence of p ensures tau transforms by sign(S_m). The two actions commute, hence product sign. This uses the actual integral presentation, not inference of action from Z/3 abstract type or mod-three sample data.
residual_risks: Jonsson known sign for m=5: this special case is covered, not an independent contribution; novelty is the all-m full sign together with H-fixed profiles.
The column sign depends on natural ordered exterior basis in the primary relative presentation, not only abstract Z3 isomorphism; future validation of its functoriality remains prudent.
No claim to complete S5 symmetry when m=5, full free homology modules, or coherent equivariant splitting.
